enumeration_note: Intro/overview video (part 1 of 6) teaching one ORB skeleton but two genuinely different entry triggers: a straight breakout entry (own stop = half-range, own targets = half/full range) and a pullback entry (re-entry to the pullback level after the break, exit gestural) â€” enumerated as two strategies per the under-split rule. The 5/15/30-minute ranges are timeframe variants of the breakout skeleton, grouped as variants.

coaching_notes: Use the first 5/15/30-minute ranges to study who is controlling â€” bulls or bears â€” and what direction the market is trending.
Understanding the psychology of these breakouts (range high = where sellers defended, range low = where buyers defended) can help transform your trading.
Watch for accelerating momentum after a breakout â€” some moves start to accelerate.
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: opening range is measured in the first 5 / 15 / 30 minutes after the 9:30 ET open
ENTRY: breakout above the opening-range high (long) or below the opening-range low (short) â€” a penny beyond the level counts as the break
STOP: half-range stop placed below the half-range mark
TARGET: half-range target = opening-range high + half the range value (e.g. OR high + ~$0.52)
TARGET: full-range target = opening-range high + full range value (e.g. OR high + $1.03)
VARIANT SUB-MECHANIC: 5-minute OR (9:30-9:35), 15-minute OR (9:30-9:45), 30-minute OR (9:30-10:00) â€” three separate ranges to read intraday control
SELECTION: setups are sought throughout the entire trading day off these ranges, not only the first 30 minutes
strategies.entry_summary: After the opening range forms (first 5, 15, or 30 minutes from the 9:30 ET open), enter on a breakout: go long when price breaks a penny above the opening-range high (buyers overcome the sellers who defended the high), or short when price breaks below the opening-range low. The break direction is the initial directional conviction.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop is the 'half-range stop' placed below the half-range mark; profit targets are the 'half-range target' (opening-range high + half the range value) and the 'full-range target' (opening-range high + the full range value). Levels are day-relative, computed from that day's opening range.
strategies.name: opening_range_breakout

variants.target_note: half-range and full-range targets off the 5m range value
variants.transcript_quote: The 5m minute OB takes place from 9:30 a.m. Eastern to 9:35 a.m. Eastern.

variants.target_note: half-range and full-range targets off the 15m range value
variants.transcript_quote: The 15-minute is the first 15 minutes of the market. So, from 9:30 to now 9:45.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: breakout above/below the 30-minute range (worked example: OR high 617.64, OR low 616.61, range $1.03)
variants.target_note: half-range target = OR high + ~$0.52; full-range target = OR high + $1.03
variants.transcript_quote: the difference between the high and the low is what gives us our opening range breakout range... In this case, the difference was a dollar 3.

element_inventory: PRECONDITION: the initial breakout must have already taken place before a pullback entry is valid
ENTRY: price pulls back to the pullback level (opening-range high âˆ’ half range) and re-enters toward the long mark
LEVEL: pullback level = opening-range high minus the half-range value (the half-range mark as an actual price)
strategies.entry_summary: After the initial opening-range breakout occurs, wait for price to pull back to the 'pullback level' (opening-range high minus the half range, e.g. OR high âˆ’ $0.52), then enter back toward the long mark in the breakout direction. Described as a full, separate 'pullback setup' distinct from the straight breakout.
strategies.exit_summary: Gestural in this intro video â€” the pullback level anchors the entry, but explicit stop/target levels for the pullback variant are not stated (the platform's half-range/full-range framework is the stated exit machinery).
strategies.name: opening_range_pullback
